sentences.text: Saltoposuchus was a small, quadrupedal reptile belonging to the Sphenosuchia group, measuring about one meter in length.
Its name translates to "leaping foot crocodile," reflecting its long, pointed skull and sharp, flattened teeth suited for a carnivorous diet.
Fossil evidence suggests this animal was likely fast and nimble.
Paleontologists conclude it was a terrestrial animal based on its fossil remains.
The species Saltoposuchus connectens and Saltoposuchus longipes were named by Friedrich von Huene in 1921 after fossils found in the Burrer Quarry.
It is debated whether Terrestrisuchus is a juvenile synonym of Saltoposuchus, as anatomical differences have been identified despite similarities.
This reptile lived during the Late Triassic Period, approximately 215.6 to 212.0 million years ago, within the supercontinent Laurasia in Europe.
The estimated time range for Saltoposuchus spans between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
